newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia urges vigilance on currency speculators.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia urges vigilance on currency speculators.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto on Friday urged the country's top finance officials to exercise caution and take steps to prevent currency speculation.

"We must always be cautious. So I am asking monetary officials such as the finance minister (Mar'ie Muhammad) and the central bank governor (Sudrajad Djiwandono) to watch the situation and take steps before the speculators can take advantage if it," State Secretary Murdiono quoted Suharto as saying.
Murdiono and the finance minister were speaking to reporters after a meeting with Suharto.
"I can say there is no use in (currency) speculation because the government will always take steps to anticipate this," Murdiono added.

Mar'ie said the latest volatility in the rupiah was not significant. "The attack on the rupiah by speculators is minimal compared to other currencies, especially the (Thai) Baht and the (Philippines) Peso."
He said this was because Indonesia had for a long time conducted a managed float of the rupiah, "so we let the market decide".
The rupiah weakened in morning trade on Friday, being quoted at 2,492.00/5.000 at 0610 GMT from an opening 2,372/75.
Southeast Asian currencies have been rattled recently by the de facto devaluations of the baht and peso. The devaluations followed weeks of speculative attacks pn both currencies.
